subject: Post-demo: QuickPulse usage buckets, burn gap, and commitment options
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily@quickpulse.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: QuickPulse usage buckets, burn gap, and commitment options

Hi Emily — great to meet you and Raj on today's demo. Quick recap (so we all have the same baseline) and three asks to get pricing locked down: 

Summary from our notes:
- Primary workload: low-latency chat assistant for support agents (avg response length ~60 tokens, 18k queries/day currently in pilot).
- Projected ramp: pilot -> prod in 6 months with expected steady-state of 550M tokens/month; peak windows up to ~900M tokens/month during product launches.
- Current QuickPulse target cost: <$750 per 1M tokens (we heard $600–$800 range on the call).

Three asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm target budget range for year-1 committed usage (monthly or annual)? a bracket like $6k–$20k / month is fine — we only need a directional number to model discounts.
2) Please attach the monthly token estimate you showed (we named it QuickPulse_monthly_token_estimates.csv) and mark which months are likely to be spike months.
3) Are you pursuing our Startup Program (early-stage credit + 30% off list for first 6 months) or would you prefer a committed-usage discount (3–12 month term with graduated bands)?

What we can do right away: Ben (cc'd) can prepare a compact commitment proposal with three tiers: Starter (no commit, pay-as-you-go with modest startup credit), Committed-3mo (monthly commit, 15–22% unit discount depending on volume), and Committed-12mo (multi-year price smoothing + 25–35% depending on size). We'll include modeled $/1M tokens for each tier given your numbers.

If you can reply to the three asks above by EOD Thursday (5/6), we'll shoot over a proposal and an optional DocuSign pre-agreement for quick review.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting this over the line.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: QuickPulse_monthly_token_estimates.csv (CSV, 12 rows)
Attachment: Redwood_commitment_options_v2.pdf (PDF)

From: Emily Park <emily@quickpulse.ai>

Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: QuickPulse usage buckets, burn gap, and commitment options

Thanks Sean — good recap. Quick answers inline: 

1) Budget range: for year-1 we have a target ops budget of roughly $15k–$25k / month for LLM inference; if incentives/commits lower the unit cost materially we could push to the high end.
2) Attached the token estimates you requested (see QuickPulse_monthly_token_estimates.csv). Note: months 4 and 9 are product launch spikes (x2.5 baseline).
3) We are eligible for Redwood's Startup Program but we'd prefer committed pricing if the math works out; leadership prefers predictable unit cost and a committed budget.

Small ask: can you provide a modeled $/1M tokens under the Committed-3mo and Committed-12mo options using our steady-state 550M/month and a launch-month 900M? If you include total monthly cost and savings vs PAYG that will help our CFO.

Happy to hop on a 20m call with Ben if needed.

—Emily
Emily Park
Head of Product, QuickPulse
emily@quickpulse.ai

Attachment: QuickPulse_monthly_token_estimates.csv (CSV)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily@quickpulse.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: QuickPulse usage buckets, burn gap, and commitment options

Emily — thanks for the clear answers and the CSV. I attached a short pricing workbook (Redwood_commitment_options_v2.pdf) and included a modeled sheet below (high level, numbers rounded):

Model assumptions used:
- PAYG list: $1,050 / 1M tokens for the large-response chat profile (baseline token mix applied).
- Starter credit: $5k one-time credit applied over first 2 months.
- Committed-3mo: 15% discount at 300M–600M buckets; 22% at 601M–1B buckets.
- Committed-12mo: 25% discount at 300M–600M; 32% at 601M–1B; additional 3% multi-year incentive at >9M tokens annualized.

Using your steady-state / launch assumptions:
- Steady-state 550M/mo: PAYG = $577.5k / month; Committed-3mo (~15% avg) ≈ $491.9k / month ($~892 / 1M tokens); Committed-12mo (~25% avg) ≈ $433.1k / month ($~787 / 1M tokens).
- Launch month 900M: PAYG = $945k; Committed-3mo (22%) ≈ $737.1k; Committed-12mo (32%) ≈ $642.6k.

These are rough but directionally accurate; I can run a more granular blended token-profile calc if you send the CSV with per-query token breakdown (request/response).

Next steps:
- If these numbers look in the ballpark, we can convert the 12-month lane into a formal SOW with monthly commit and an option to rebaseline after Q2.
- If you want to move fast, I can open a DocuSign with a non-binding letter-of-intent for the 12mo commit so your finance team can see the payment schedule.

Would Emily and Raj be available Monday 5/10 for a 20m call to finalize which lane to pursue?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: Redwood_commitment_options_v2.pdf (PDF)

From: Raj Patel <raj@quickpulse.ai>

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: QuickPulse usage buckets, burn gap, and commitment options

Thanks Ben — numbers look promising and closer to what we need. Quick notes from finance side: 
- CFO prefers committed-12mo if we can get to ~$700–$750 per 1M tokens effective (annualized) for the steady-state band; that would allow us to reallocate budget for model evaluation later in year.
- We also need a short clause in the SOW for a one-time rebaseline after the first 90 days if actuals deviate >25%.

Happy to take a quick call Monday to confirm lane; if Redwood can provide a sample SOW and a high-level payment schedule (monthly invoicing, early termination language, rebaseline clause) we'll circulate to CFO for verbal approval.

If you can, prepare the DocuSign LOI for the 12mo lane at the ~$700/1M effective target and include the 90-day rebaseline clause. We'll review and push to finance.

—Raj

VP Engineering, QuickPulse
